findings.finding: Above the upper-right courtyard window, a bounded red-brown patch with horizontal gray mortar-like courses remains visible in colour. The source shows a soft pale/dark damaged patch without resolved brick courses at those positions. The V3 grayscale retains the source closely, so I do not claim new luminance edges; nevertheless, the chromatic pattern supplies an exposed-brick/mortar layout not supported by the source. This residual invented material detail prevents acceptance as a faithful material reference.

Courtyard openings and narrow apertures, roof/chimneys/vents, pipe, adjacent balconies and laundry, tree/trunk/branches, shed remnants and cloth, graffiti, steps, debris and foreground platform are retained.
The circular chalk mark by the lower opening and neighboring small marks remain at source-level legibility. No house identity is inferred from them.

Rear green joinery versus front brown joinery is not treated as inconsistency without dated entity evidence. The rejection concerns the specific unsupported brick-course colour pattern above the window.

Matched dimensions and very close grayscale structure support the visual preservation findings but are not a visual pass or proof of historical colours. Chroma-only material patterns must be judged in colour.
